message.content:
The number of distinct legal positions that can arise in a standard game of chess is astronomically large – on the order of **10⁴³**.  

This figure, often called the *Shannon number*, was first estimated by Claude Shannon in 1950 and represents a lower bound on the true count. Modern research suggests the actual number of legal positions may be closer to **10⁴⁶**, but the exact value remains unknown because enumerating all possibilities is computationally infeasible.
